authority: DiscoveryKnowledge in PlayableCampaignState, schema 10 discovery v1. Scenario map catalogue supplies names and membership. Command rights and RPG treasure authority remain separate.

broaderRequirements.text: Visiting a settlement or accepting a quest there is sufficient to record that settlement as known for later navigation.
Quest/map assistance must not reveal unrelated undiscovered geography, hidden locations, secret objectives, or information the quest intentionally withholds.
A quest may reveal an exact destination, only a region, an approximate search area, or no marker at all according to its scenario data.

Revealing general fog-of-war or exploring a region does not automatically identify every hidden point of interest inside it; precise quest markers require that the destination itself is known or has been explicitly revealed by the quest/clue.
The world/region map should support centering or focusing on a known named settlement/location without physically moving the player's character.

closedPortions.scope: Validated settlement visits, including questless interactions and local quest acceptance, persist as exact knowledge.
World and regional settlement listings expose only authorized knowledge; invalid requests preserve the current view.
General region discovery reveals neither unvisited settlements nor hidden points of interest.
The registered map focus action accepts known named settlements without changing party, orders or command context.
Region and visited-settlement authority survives saves, fresh reconstruction, physical travel, remote command and return.

executedTests.validates: Validated questless visits, named world/regional filtering, exact focus, pause ownership and unchanged party/orders/context.
Wrong-map, distant, stale, malformed and unavailable interactions reject without knowledge; aliases record canonical IDs.
Multiple visits, failed storage, fresh services, travel, return and preserved treasure resolution/precision.
Physical remote command and return preserve absent home-party coordinates and do not invent visits or command rights.
Schemas 1–9 preserve recorded IDs; empty legacy discovery invents no visits; invalid and duplicate current records reject.
Late reconstruction failure restores knowledge/projections and retains modal/manual pause ownership.
